items.excerpt: The 35th IPA Congress in Kuala Lumpur closed on an optimistic note, wrapping days of AI-dominated sessions with final-day discussions on AI's impact on publishing, global literacy, and freedom to publish. Distinct closing-day substance beyond earlier congress coverage.
items.note: IPA Congress already covered 7/8, but this is the closing-day wrap with new substance (final-day sessions, closing remarks). Curator should verify it adds enough beyond the 7/8 card.

items.excerpt: At the IPA Congress closing gala, two AI companies won the IPA Innovation in Publishing Award: Shimmr, which built an autonomous subscription-based 'Advertising as a Service' AI platform for continuous book marketing, and Ailaysa, a multilingual AI company behind the Chai Reader discovery platform.
items.note: IPA-adjacent but a distinct, concrete development: AI companies winning publishing's innovation award. Strong tool/workflow hook (AI book marketing + multilingual publishing AI).

items.excerpt: Jamir Nazir won the 2026 Commonwealth Short Story Prize for 'The Serpent in the Grove' after AI-use allegations against the Granta-published story triggered an unprecedented competition-wide review that ultimately cleared the regional winner.
items.note: First major literary prize decided after a formal AI review — new precedent for how awards handle AI allegations. Related Lithub allegation piece is from May (stale); this June 30 resolution is the fresh story.

items.excerpt: Amazon's Kindle Recaps — AI-generated, spoiler-free 'previously on...' summaries of series and in-progress books — is now accessible via an internet browser, expanding the feature beyond Kindle devices and apps.
items.note: Kindle Recaps is Amazon's genAI recap feature; keyword pool lists 'Kindle Recaps expansion'. Second Good e-Reader item (per-source cap 3 OK).

items.excerpt: 중국 무료 웹소설 플랫폼들이 AI 생성 소설을 AI로 판별해 대규모 단속(한 달 10만권 이상 계약 거부)에 나서면서, 인간 작가들이 되레 'AI처럼 보이지 않는 글쓰기'를 고민해야 하는 역설이 벌어지고 있다.
